answer: Divergent History Challenge. Each identity must publish a signed action log whose kernel includes a random nonce from a shared beacon. Clones replaying one history produce identical logs, so a verifier will challenge any two accounts whose logs match at a checkpoint and then demand divergent follow-up actions. Honest agents diverge naturally; clones cannot. An attacker must run each clone as a separate agent with distinct state, paying full compute and an ember of registration work per identity. Matching logs at any summit review flags and voids the batch.
